name: Croatia

train.sum: Zagreb Glavni kolodvor (main station) is the only passenger terminus. HZPP runs trains to Split, Rijeka, Osijek and Croatian towns, plus trains to Ljubljana, Vienna, Budapest and night trains to Zurich and Stuttgart.
train.sched: Trains leave from early morning until late evening. Some lines have only a few trains a day, so check times on prodaja.hzpp.hr. A new timetable year starts in December.
tickets: Zagreb to Split by Intercity: about 28 EUR in 2nd class, advance fares from about 15 EUR, plus a seat reservation from 1.06 EUR
Zagreb to Ljubljana: Ljubljana Spezial 9 EUR one way, 18 EUR return (2nd class)
Zagreb to Ljubljana to Pula: 24 EUR one way
Night train to Stuttgart or Zurich: seat from about 29 EUR, 6-berth couchette from about 49 EUR, 2-berth sleeper from about 89 EUR
Online tickets are 10 percent cheaper than at the ticket office. Children and many students and pensioners travel on discounts or free with a card
train.tip: Seat reservations are compulsory on Intercity trains to the coast, so book ahead for summer.
buy: HZPP app or online at prodaja.hzpp.hr: e-tickets are 10 percent cheaper than at the counter
Ticket office at Zagreb Glavni kolodvor, open every day 05:20 to 21:40
Ticket machines for domestic tickets at Zagreb main station and other large stations
International tickets at the HZPP international ticket offices
On board you can pay by contactless card, but the ticket costs 10 percent more than at the office
Boarding without a ticket and not reporting to the conductor: surcharge of 66.36 EUR plus the fare, or 33.18 EUR if paid within 3 days

destinations.note: Weekdays only on the direct regional trains
Daily afternoon train. A second train runs via Ljubljana
Direct on Fridays via Ljubljana. Return from Pula on Sundays
Daily afternoon train. A summer morning train takes about 7 h. A night train also runs
Several trains a day. Slower trains take up to 2 h 45 min
Leaves about 08:40. Change here for Salzburg and Munich
Intercity 201, one daily train to Budapest-Deli via Koprivnica. Seat reservation is optional but recommended
Leaves about 19:39. From 7 Feb to 8 Jul 2027 it leaves earlier
Leaves about 19:39 with sleeper and couchette cars. Also serves Salzburg

tram.sum: ZET runs the blue Zagreb trams on about 120 km of track, plus buses, the Uspinjaca funicular and the Sljeme cable car. Zagreb has no metro.
tram.sched: Day trams and buses run from early morning to late evening, and night tram and night bus lines run after that. Line times are on zet.hr.
tickets: 30-minute ticket (day service): 0.53 EUR from kiosks and the app, 0.80 EUR from the driver
60-minute ticket: 0.93 EUR from kiosks and the app, 1.33 EUR from the driver
90-minute ticket: 1.33 EUR from kiosks and the app, 1.99 EUR from the driver
Multi-day tickets for 3, 7, 15 or 30 days: only at ZET ticket offices, check zet.hr for prices
tram.tip: Buy at a Tisak kiosk or in the Moj ZET app. The driver price is higher, and you must validate your ticket on board.
buy: Tisak and iNovine kiosks near most stops (ask for a tramvajska karta)
Moj ZET app: top up from 1 EUR, up to 50 EUR in the wallet. Show the QR code to inspectors
ZET ticket offices at main stops and terminals (multi-day tickets are sold only here)
From the driver, at the higher price, for 30, 60 and 90 minute tickets and day tickets
Contactless bank card payment on board is planned for summer 2027
Fine without a valid ticket: 66.36 to 106.18 EUR. Paying 33.18 EUR early avoids court proceedings

bus.sum: ZET runs 136 daytime bus lines and 5 night lines across Zagreb, Velika Gorica and Zaprešic. Long-distance coaches leave from the main bus station (Autobusni kolodvor).
bus.sched: Day lines run from early morning to late evening, and five night bus lines cover the hours after that. Timetables are on zet.hr.
tickets: ZET bus: same fare as the tram, 0.53 EUR for 30 minutes, 0.93 EUR for 60 minutes, 1.33 EUR for 90 minutes
Day ticket: 3.98 EUR for trams and buses in zone 1
Zagreb Card: free ZET travel in zone 1 (the funicular and cable car are not included)
bus.tip: Zagreb city is zone 1 and the airport and Velika Gorica are in zone 2. A bus to the airport needs two 30-minute tickets.
buy: Tisak and iNovine kiosks (cheaper than the driver)
Moj ZET app on Android and iOS
ZET ticket offices
From the driver at the higher price. Drivers rarely have change
Long-distance coaches: buy at the bus station or online

airport.sum: Franjo Tudman Airport (ZAG) is in Pleso, about 17 km south of the centre. Pleso Prijevoz buses run to the main bus station, and ZET bus 290 runs to Kvaternikov trg.
airport.sched: Pleso Prijevoz runs about every 30 minutes in the day, with extra buses after late flights. ZET bus 290 runs about every 35 minutes and takes about 35 minutes. Check the operator's timetable for first and last departures.
tickets: Pleso Prijevoz bus to the main bus station: 8 EUR one way, 16 EUR return
ZET bus 290 to Kvaternikov trg: two 30-minute tickets at 0.53 EUR each
Taxi and ride hailing (Uber, Bolt): check the fare before you ride
Children under 7 travel free on Pleso Prijevoz
airport.tip: Bus 290 is the cheapest way in, and Pleso Prijevoz is faster and goes straight to the bus and train stations area.
buy: Pleso Prijevoz: from the driver (cash) or online on plesoprijevoz.hr
ZET bus 290: Tisak kiosks in the arrival and departure halls, or the Moj ZET app
Validate the first ticket when you board and the second after crossing the Sava river
Taxi: licensed taxi rank outside arrivals, or the Uber or Bolt app

metro.note: Zagreb has no metro. The blue tram network is the backbone of the city, with day lines and night lines, plus buses, a funicular and a cable car.
metro.mapLabel: ZET tram and bus network maps and timetables
lines: Trams run on about 120 km of track, with day lines and night lines
Ban Jelacic Square is the centre of the tram network
Zagreb Glavni kolodvor (train station) and the main bus station are both on tram lines
The Uspinjaca funicular climbs to the Upper Town and reopened on 19 May 2026
The Sljeme cable car runs from Gracansko dolje to Sljeme mountain

tips: Contactless card payment is not on trams yet, so buy a ticket at a kiosk or in the Moj ZET app before you board.
Validate your ticket when you board. Inspectors may wear plain clothes and fines start at 66.36 EUR.
The Zagreb Card gives free ZET travel in zone 1 but does not cover the airport, funicular or cable car.
Train tickets bought on board cost 10 percent more, so buy them in the HZPP app or at the station.
